prompt: imagemagick remap colormap precision bit depth limit
answer:
ImageMagick’s `-remap` has a **maximum colormap precision of 8 bits**. If the remap image contains deeper-precision colors, ImageMagick automatically coalesces them to satisfy this limit.

This is separate from `-depth`, which specifies the number of bits per channel for image pixels. For example, 16-bit RGB channels range from 0 to 65,535, but that does not increase the precision supported by a `-remap` colormap.

The remapped colors are selected in RGB space, unless dithering is enabled; dithering is enabled by default.

Source: [ImageMagick command-line options](https://imagemagick.org/command-line-options/)
